archetype: Aristocrats-combo, and strategic_frame.json's 'combo' label is the right one — the audit's archetype overrides (tutors 4-8, protection 4-6) fit. But the deck's own verified artifacts describe something narrower: a value engine with one unbounded kill attached. Five of the eight checker-passed stacks run the Yawgmoth + Nest of Scarabs engine and every one of them terminates by body exhaustion inside a single main phase. Only stack 001's Blowfly Infestation + Nest of Scarabs + a drain (plus two spare bodies) is verified unbounded.
verdict: It functions and it draws its pieces. 36 lands, a 0.923 turn-3 land-drop rate, 43 black sources against a Karsten target of 36, and every declared enabler class above 0.60 by turn 10 with one exception: fast mana, at 0.435 on three cards. That exception stays open, and nothing prescribed below closes it: Cabal Coffers and Urborg are mana VOLUME, not fast mana — Coffers produces nothing until you can pay {2} and control Swamps, and Urborg alone adds no mana at all. Whether the turn-2 line is worth a spell slot is queued as an open question rather than answered here. What limits the deck is conversion: four declared kills, one verified. Stacks 002, 003, 004, 005 and 008 all measured the Yawgmoth engine ending by body exhaustion at 8 to 52 pod life against 160, and the only line the checker passed as unbounded (001) rests on Blowfly Infestation, a single card measured at 0.026 unassisted. Nest of Scarabs is named in all eight passing stacks and the audit's combo route finds no card in the pool that joins it.

single_points_of_failure.why: Stacks 002, 003, 004 and 005 (all pass) measured the same arithmetic: once your own creatures are taking the counters, each activation costs two bodies and Nest returns one, so the engine is body-negative and terminates. Opponents' creatures are the only free counter sinks — 002 and 003 both found a 2/2 Grizzly Bears EXTENDS the engine by two activations. CORRECTION: the previous version of this entry called the class undeclared and empty. It is neither. Gravecrawler ('You may cast this card from your graveyard as long as you control a Zombie', {B}) is a NAMED HALF of THE FOURTH KILL, so the deck's own goldfish targets already declare in-loop recursion; Reassembling Skeleton ('{1}{B}: Return this card from your graveyard to the battlefield tapped') and Butcher Ghoul (undying, one shot) are in the 99 as well, and the first two also sit in the fodder component listed above. The correct reading is that the class is thin and CONDITIONAL, not absent. Gravecrawler needs a Zombie on the battlefield — Warren Soultrader is a Zombie Goblin Wizard, Grave Titan makes 2/2 Zombies, Nim Deathmantle makes the equipped creature a black Zombie — so the condition is satisfiable inside this deck but is not free; Reassembling Skeleton costs {1}{B} a body against mean available mana 5.228 on turn 6. None of the four passing stacks held either card, so they bound a board, not the deck. Of the pool: Pawn of Ulamog reads 'another nontoken creature you control dies', so Insect tokens never trigger it, and Forsaken Miner's return is gated on committing a crime, which needs an opponent-facing target — precisely the case the stacks say already extends the engine and which is absent once the counters land on your own bodies. Neither is a closer here. Nether Traitor is the unconditional version, and it is a cost-and-reliability upgrade on two incumbents rather than the filling of an empty class.

open_questions.question: Does Nether Traitor loop mana-neutrally off token deaths? Specifically: a 1/1 Insect dies to its own -1/-1 counter, Phyrexian Altar or Pitiless Plunderer produces mana from that death, and that mana pays Nether Traitor's {B} return — is the trigger condition 'another creature is put into your graveyard from the battlefield' satisfied by a token that 704.5f puts there before 704.5d removes it, and does the timing let the mana arrive before the return is paid?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the exact bound stacks 002, 003, 004 and 005 all hit — the engine ends because bodies do not come back. If this holds, it is the only structural fix in the pool; if it does not, the add above is a 1/1 with shadow and should be withdrawn.

open_questions.question: Are Mikaeus, the Unhallowed + Ashnod's Altar, + Phyrexian Altar, + Carrion Feeder and + Viscera Seer real two-card infinites in this deck, and what ends each?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The Carnifex Demon cut no longer rests on this — that reason is withdrawn above precisely because these lines are unverified. It still matters on its own: Mikaeus carries seven of the deck's eleven recorded two-card infinites, those eleven are what bracket-check uses to force floor 4, and THE SECOND KILL is declared on him. If they fail the way the Yawgmoth lines failed, the deck has fewer kills than it declares and a lower floor than it reports.

open_questions.question: Do the archetype's between-turns fodder engines (Ophiomancer, and Bitterblossom which is already in the 99) contribute anything to a loop that terminates inside one main phase? Should goldfish_targets.json separate 'a fodder card drawn' from 'bodies available during the loop'?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The RENEWABLE FODDER target measures 0.736 and is labelled the bottleneck, while the stacks say the deck runs out of bodies mid-chain. Those cannot both be the same quantity, and until the target distinguishes them no measurement can adjudicate recon's top finding.

open_questions.question: Does the 'Fast mana' target's any_of (Sol Ring, Ancient Tomb, Dark Ritual) understate the deck once Culling the Weak or Jet Medallion is in the 99, given that goldfish explicitly does not model cost reducers or rituals beyond the named three?
open_questions.why_it_matters: 0.435 is the thinnest measured component and is driving a mana-package recommendation. If the target is simply narrow, the recommendation is sized wrong in one direction or the other, and widening the target is a goldfish_targets.json edit plus a re-run, not a claim this diagnosis can make.

open_questions.question: Does Drivnod, Carnage Dominus double Mirkwood Bats? Bats triggers on 'you create or sacrifice a token'; Drivnod's replacement is worded around 'a creature dying'.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Carried unresolved from considering.json's gaps. Stack 008 measured Bats at 13 triggers and 52 pod life — the deck's largest verified damage figure — so whether Drivnod doubles it decides whether Drivnod is a five-mana build-around or a five-mana blank.

open_questions.question: Does Nim Deathmantle + Ashnod's Altar loop in this 99, and at what mana? The Altar adds {C}{C} and the Deathmantle return costs {4}, so the recorded two-card line is two mana short per iteration and needs a third piece — is there one in the deck (Pitiless Plunderer, Phyrexian Altar, Warren Soultrader), and does the resulting loop produce anything other than triggers?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The Nim Deathmantle cut is priced on losing this package. combo_details.json records it as infinite triggers, not infinite mana, and nothing here is checker-passed. If the package needs a third piece, the cut is cheaper than stated; if it loops on two, the cut is more expensive and Deathmantle should be re-argued.

open_questions.question: Should this deck spend a spell slot on turn-1/2 fast mana at all? The 'Fast mana' target (Sol Ring, Ancient Tomb, Dark Ritual) measures 0.435 assembled and 0.348 by turn 6, and the deck's own label calls it 'the turn-2-Yawgmoth enabler' — but goldfish_metrics.json casts the commander on turn 2 in 707 of 10,000 games, with a mean cast turn of 4.283. The draw rate and the turn-2 line are two different quantities and no artifact here reconciles them.
open_questions.why_it_matters: 0.435 is the thinnest measured component in the deck and this diagnosis prescribes nothing that touches it — the previous pass claimed two lands did, and they do not. Either the deck should buy the turn-2 line with a slot (recon finding 3, as_of 2026-08-03, names Jet Medallion at 74.2% and Culling the Weak at 45.5% as how the archetype does it), or the target measures an outcome this build has chosen not to chase and the thinness is a decision rather than a hole. A goldfish run reporting the commander's turn-2 cast rate with and without a fast-mana add would settle it; a diagnosis cannot. This is distinct from the question above about the any_of being too narrow.

gaps: THE OPHIOMANCER COLLISION RESOLVES ON TRIBE, NOT ON TIMING — and my first argument for it was wrong twice. deck_recon.json finding 1 (as_of 2026-08-03) names Ophiomancer at 73.5% of 6,961 EDHREC lists as one of the two fodder engines this deck lacks; considering.json excludes it because South Wind Avatar is Creature — Snake Spirit Avatar, the only Snake in the 100, so Ophiomancer's 'if you control no Snakes' clause makes it create nothing at all while the Avatar is on the battlefield. That reading is decisive, not merely correct, because the board it blanks on is the board the deck most wants: the Avatar is Exquisite Blood's only partner in the 99 (bracket-check names 'Exquisite Blood + South Wind Avatar' as the deck's highest-bracket line), it is the payoff stack 005 (pass) measured at 28 pod life, and its 4 toughness is the counter sink the same stack priced at exactly +4 activations. Cutting the Avatar to make Ophiomancer live would orphan a checker-passed stack and delete the deck's combo_content driver. I previously rested this on timing instead, and two things in that argument were false: Ophiomancer triggers at the beginning of EACH upkeep, so in a five-player pod it is up to five Snakes a turn cycle rather than one per turn; and stack 007 does NOT terminate by body exhaustion — it halts because Mirkwood Bats' 2/3 survives the forced counter and nothing dies, leaving two Insects idle, which gaps[3] below states correctly. Whether a between-turns fodder engine contributes anything to a single-main-phase loop remains genuinely open (open_questions[3]) and the tribal blank does not depend on the answer. Recon's underlying point is right and is prescribed above in its in-loop form: Nether Traitor.

RECON FINDING 8 IS REFUTED BY ARTIFACT. It states that Exquisite Blood 'has no partner in the 99 that turns it into a kill'. bracket-check names Exquisite Blood + South Wind Avatar as the deck's highest-bracket combo line, and goldfish_targets.json declares it as THE THIRD KILL with a measured 0.029 unassisted / 0.325 assisted. The finding's card list (Sanguine Bond, Marauding Blight-Priest, Vito, Bloodthirsty Conqueror) is still useful as redundancy, but exactly ONE of the four is prescribed above — Marauding Blight-Priest. Sanguine Bond, Vito and Bloodthirsty Conqueror appear nowhere in the adds, and Starscape Cleric, the other drain prescribed, is not on recon's list. The finding's premise is false and no recommendation here rests on it.

THE ROLE TAXONOMY MISCLASSIFIES FOUR CARDS HERE AND THREE OF THEM MOVE AN AXIS. Necropotence is filed 'stax' alone, so the best draw engine in mono-black contributes nothing to card-advantage; Bojuka Bog is 'land:tapped', so its graveyard exile is invisible to interaction-breadth; Supernatural Stamina has no card_roles entry at all and Malakir Rebirth is 'ramp:ritual', and both grant a dies-trigger return, i.e. protection. Corrected: card-advantage is functionally ~11 (not 5) and protection is 5 (not 3), and only interaction-breadth survives as a real hole. The audit's own probe note catches five of these cards; Necropotence and Bojuka Bog are not among them. The fix is a ROLE_PATTERNS edit plus `manamap card-roles`, not a decklist change, and it is out of scope for a read-only diagnosis.

NO PAINFUL CUT WAS DODGED, AND ONE WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED. Carnifex Demon is recommended knowing it deletes THE SECOND KILL outright and removes the deck's only repeatable mass ignition. The alternative painful cut examined was Mirkwood Bats: stack 007 (pass) proved Bats HALTS the Blowfly loop — the deck's only verified unbounded kill — because its 2/3 body survives the forced counter and nothing dies. It is not recommended, because stack 007's board held two creatures and stack 001's own prescription (the drain plus two spare bodies) removes the halt; recommending a cut on a board-specific artefact would be over-claiming. Stack 008 also measured Bats at 13 triggers and 52 pod life, the deck's largest verified damage number.

NOT ONE OF THE 42 CONTAINED COMBO LINES IS VERIFIED AS A KILL except stack 001's Blowfly + Nest + a drain with two spare bodies. Eleven are two-card infinites by Commander Spellbook's tagging and the checker has already refuted that tagging twice on this deck (stacks 001 and 005 both say so in as many words). Every combo line named in an add above carries 'needs a stack scenario' and none is priced as a win.

THE UNION OF FOUR KILLS IS NOT A NUMBER ANYONE HAS. The audit says so itself — the target schema is an AND of ORs and cannot express 'any one of four independent kills'. The closest measured proxy is 'EITHER kill assembled' at 0.055 unassisted / 0.328 assisted, and it covers only two of the four. So 'how often does this deck assemble something lethal' is unanswered, and the verdict above is deliberately phrased against what the stacks measured rather than against an aggregate that does not exist.

PRICES ARE STRIPPED from cards.csv, so nothing here weighs acquisition cost. Of the seven adds, three are already on this deck's bench (Cabal Coffers, Urborg, Imp's Mischief) and considering.json records Urborg as owned via share/Hapatra.txt; the other four are purchases of unknown size.

RECON IS DATED AND ITS PERCENTAGES CANNOT BE RE-DERIVED HERE. No artifact in this repo carries per-commander inclusion rates — docs/deck-builder-v2.md names that hole explicitly — so 73.5%, 81.4% and 54.2% are carried as evidence from an as_of 2026-08-03 external source, never as measurement, and no axis verdict above rests on one.

FOUR RECON FINDINGS ARE LEFT UNPRESCRIBED AND SHOULD NOT BE READ AS REJECTED. Reanimation as a second tutor layer (Reanimate, Entomb), Jet Medallion as colour-specific cost reduction, Liliana Dreadhorde General as the archetype's top-end, and the six Game Changers of the combo-tagged subset all cost slots this diagnosis spent on the drain class and on interaction-breadth instead. Jet Medallion in particular is unpriceable until the fast-mana goldfish target is widened — see the open question.

"NO CLOSER EXISTS" IS UNMEASURED FOR EVERY ONE-CARD COMPONENT IN THIS DECK, AND THERE ARE EIGHT OF THEM — the previous version of this gap counted seven. deck-audit runs its role route only when two or more members of a component share a role or an axis, and prints so verbatim: "No role and no axis is shared by two or more members, so this component has no signature and only the combo route ran." The eight singletons and their combo-route totals are Nest of Scarabs 0, Blowfly Infestation 13, Mikaeus 119, CARNIFEX DEMON 122, Exquisite Blood 2, South Wind Avatar 8, Warren Soultrader 48, Gravecrawler 25. Carnifex was the one missing, and it carries the LARGEST count of the eight — which matters, because cut_candidates[4] removes it. It does not make that cut cheaper, and the reason is what the count actually measures: the combo route returns pool cards that complete a recorded line with a SIBLING component of the same target, never cards that perform the component's own function. Carnifex's siblings are Mikaeus and the eight-card sacrifice-outlet group; of the eight lines the audit prints, only three name Mikaeus at all (Altar of Dementia; Carrion Feeder + Plague Belcher; Walking Ballista), none names Carnifex, and none puts a -1/-1 counter on each other creature, which is the function the cut removes. The same property is why Blowfly's 13 are all drains. So a closer count is evidence that a SLOT has recorded neighbours, never that a FUNCTION is replaceable, and every one of those lines carries "needs a stack scenario" under gaps[4]. Whether any pool card actually replaces Carnifex's repeatable mass ignition, or Blowfly's on-death counter, is unmeasured by either route — so cut_candidates[4] stands at the price it states, and that price is not reduced by 122. Widening this would be a deck_audit.py change, not a decklist change, and it is out of scope for a read-only diagnosis.

findings.note: NEW THIS PASS, and it is the one thing three passes have missed. The diagnosis states the assembly requirement for its ONLY verified kill four separate times, always in the harder of the two forms stack 001 actually gives: archetype ("Blowfly Infestation + Nest of Scarabs + a drain (plus two spare bodies)"), this entry ("with two spare bodies on the battlefield, 38 iterations"), gaps[3] ("stack 001's own prescription (the drain plus two spare bodies)") and gaps[4] ("Blowfly + Nest + a drain with two spare bodies"). I read stack 001's build_requirement in full. It is explicitly TWO cases. Case (1), which is what the diagnosis reports, is the CREATURE-drain case: "the board must hold the drain creature PLUS TWO OTHER CREATURES when the loop starts... three creatures total." Case (2) is the NONCREATURE-drain case: "the board needs the counter-bearing creature PLUS ONE OTHER CREATURE, because the drain itself is not a legal target and so can never be eaten. Bastion of Remembrance is the right card because it satisfies BOTH halves of case (2): it is an Enchantment, so Blowfly cannot target it, AND its enters-the-battlefield trigger... supplies the one other creature itself." Bastion of Remembrance IS in the 99 — it is the FIRST card listed in engine.components[3] (payoff, 6 cards, 0.669) — and I confirmed its oracle text from cards.csv: "When this enchantment enters, create a 1/1 white Human Soldier creature token. Whenever a creature you control dies, each opponent loses 1 life and you gain 1 life." So on the deck's own cards the requirement is Blowfly + Nest + Bastion + one counter-bearing creature, and the ignition class that supplies the last of those measures 0.730. The word "Bastion" appears twice in the whole diagnosis and neither mention is about this. The direction of the error matters: the diagnosis's central thesis is "what limits the deck is conversion", and it prices its only verified unbounded kill as strictly harder to assemble than the checker-passed stack it cites says it is. Nothing else in the entry is wrong — the 38 iterations, the 0.026/0.321 rates and the 'no closer is offered' conclusion all check out.

NEW THIS PASS.
